# Raw Compression Study: Summary (Phase 1 + Phase 2)

**Date:** 2026-10-01, overnight, unattended (Nick: "run the tests once you get consensus … then move to on-hardware testing").
**Data:** S4 session 1 (2026-09-30, nereus002): V1 card + Pixel Perfect chart at 0.5 m, two LED lamps (cool, warm 3200 K), 3 locked repeats per stop, all three cameras. The same frames were also made red-starved *at capture* (red × 0.14, blue × 0.8, binomial thinning) to stand in for 15 m of water.
**Full report:** https://claude.ai/artifact/8MgizMsuEpo1xJC6cgdwQr (private; also `results/report.html`, regenerated by `python -m compression_study.report`): charts, crops, inventory, method explanations. **All rows:** `results/results.csv` (1,193 rows).

## Answer

**Yes. Raw Bayer data compresses to today's budget and keeps colour clearly better than today's JPEG pipeline, on all three cameras.** The best method is **D2** (square-root curve → 4 Bayer planes → JPEG XL, modular mode); on red-starved OpenMV frames at 0.4 bpp it is **L** (the repo's 2×2-binned linear JPEG XL).

Mean stress ΔE2000 (WB + colour matrix, red ×4), best raw method vs today's JPEG (M1):

| | 0.4 bpp (≈ 50 kB/MP) | 0.8 bpp | vs the *best* processed codec (often jpegli or M1-fix) |
|---|---|---|---|
| IMX708 | **−83 to −92 %** | −80 to −90 % | −38 to −62 % |
| N6 | −59 to −75 % | −77 to −80 % | −19 to −72 % |
| AE3 | −50 to −72 % | −54 to −75 % | −12 to −61 % |

On the IMX708 field link (the same 1600×900 crop at 50 kB), D2 is **64–81 % lower** than the deployed resized JPEG.

The gain is in **colour accuracy** (the bias of patch and region colours), not in per-pixel noise. At 0.4–0.8 bpp every codec has to drop most of the sensor's white noise; that is a rate-distortion limit, not a codec flaw. So the spec's "2× lower red error/noise" rule never fires (1.1–1.5× in air, 0.9–1.1× under water), while the stress-ΔE rule fires on every camera.

## Decision gate (spec §8, verbatim; must hold on both lamps)

| Camera | In air | Underwater-sim | Deciding comparison (best N/D/D2 variant vs M1, stress ΔE) |
|---|---|---|---|
| IMX708 | **PASS** | **PASS** | at 0.4 bpp (one at 0.8): D2 0.04–0.08 vs M1 0.43–0.78 (−85 to −92 %) |
| OpenMV N6 | **PASS** | **PASS** | at 0.8 bpp: D2 0.11–0.39 vs M1 0.49–1.79 (−77 to −80 %) |
| OpenMV AE3 | **PASS** | **PASS** | at 0.8 bpp (one at 0.4): D2 0.16–0.58 vs M1 0.57–2.05 (−53 to −73 %) |

Every pass comes from the ≥ 30 % stress-ΔE rule. The 2× red error/noise rule never passes. On red-starved OpenMV frames at 0.4 bpp, full-resolution D2/eq gains only ~10 % (N6: 1.40 vs M1 1.56); the red+ and 3-plane variants and L do much better there. 0.4 bpp is tight for full-resolution 8-bit OpenMV raw under water.

**Supporting check (pre-registered by the reviewers): FAIL on every camera.** D2/eq has **about half the block colour error** (−42 to −64 %) than the *best* processed codec (usually jpegli, not M1). But that gap (0.1–0.5 ΔE00) is smaller than the colour difference between two exposures of the same scene (0.55–1.17 ΔE00). Read it as: in these conditions the good codecs are already below shot-to-shot noise. D2's advantage is real, but on whole-frame colour it is small next to sensor noise. The large win is against **today's** pipeline (M1, and especially M1-fix, below).

**Side questions (§8):**
- **Below noise (≤ 0.5) in red at ≤ T2?** Only in the underwater-sim, at ~0.8 bpp: D2 red+2 on N6 / AE3 (0.48) and L on the IMX708 (0.45–0.50). Never at 0.4 bpp; the rate-distortion bound rules it out (≥ 0.76σ for white noise).
- **D2 vs hardware-friendly D (best of D, D-j, D-lin):** D2 is **26–87 % better** in stress ΔE, well over the 15 % threshold, so **JPEG XL is worth having**. Square root + 8-bit grayscale JPEG (D) is *worse* than today's JPEG on the 8-bit OpenMV data and on the IMX708 50 kB crop.
- **Lossless vs near-lossless:** IMX708 lossless is 3.0 bpp (JPEG XL) / 3.37 bpp (our MCU packer), vs N/b8 2.66 bpp (red error/noise 0.27, below noise) and N/b7 1.91 bpp (0.55). With the same packer, **near-lossless saves 21 % (b8) to 43 % (b7)**. On 8-bit OpenMV data lossless is cheaper than N/b8 (1.9–2.4 vs 2.8 bpp), so **use true lossless there**.

## The underwater mechanism, reproduced

M1-fix (fixed in-air white balance + colour matrix, like a real camera) on red-starved data: the matrix pushes weak red below zero and the 8-bit image clips it. Red clipped at 0: **N6 ~100 %** of pixels, AE3 2–12 %, IMX708 4–5 %. Stress ΔE at 0.4 bpp: N6 **29–38**, AE3 4–11, IMX708 2.0–2.4, vs 0.6–0.7 / 0.6–0.9 / 0.07–0.09 for the best raw method. Raw-plane coding cannot have this failure: there is no matrix before quantization. This is the TG-7 "red 0/255" failure from S2a.

## On the devices (Phase 2, nereus002)

| | IMX708 on Pi Zero 2 W (12 MP, 1 core) | OpenMV N6 (HD, live) | OpenMV AE3 (HD, live) |
|---|---|---|---|
| RAW capture | 5.9 s (`rpicam-still --raw`, DNG + JPEG) | 8.5 ms snapshot, 8-bit | same, 8-bit |
| Plane split (+ sqrt LUT) | 0.09 s (+0.4 s) numpy | 66 ms (+58 ms) viper | 118 ms (+102 ms) viper |
| D: 4 grayscale JPEGs | 0.8–1.3 s, 8 MB (cjpeg) | **26 ms q70** (hardware JPEG) | 98 ms q70 (software) |
| D2: JPEG XL | VarDCT e7 **127–142 s**, e3 10 s, ~150 MB; modular e7 **does not fit** in 250 MB | not available (no MCU encoder) | not available |
| C: lossless packer | **1.45 s, ~1 MB** (C, gcc) | **0.48 s** (viper port) | 0.86 s (viper port) |
| Bit-exact on the Mac | C, C2, N exact; D/D2 match Phase 1 | packer **bit-exact + byte-identical to packer.c**, 4/4 planes | same, 4/4 planes |
| Energy (UPS, whole rig) | ≈ +0.8–1.0 W over idle while encoding → C ≈ 1 J, D ≈ 1 J, D2 VarDCT e3 ≈ 7 J, e7 ≈ 115 J | below meter resolution (< ±0.1 W) | below meter resolution |
| Memory | 250 MB cap per encoder; parent swapped into zram (rig unaffected) | 25.6 MB heap free | **4 MB heap free**; HD RGB565 demosaic fails (MemoryError) |

Each board was reset and answered the rig handshake after every session: 0 `error -71`, 0 unexpected reboots (OQ-53 note). The final `scripts/test_openmv_raw.sh` captured and transferred on both boards. Its two brightness-plausibility asserts failed only because the room was dark at 03:00 (mean 4.3 DN at 24 dB).

## Recommendation

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| **D2 (sqrt + JPEG XL modular), backend decode** | Best colour at every size and camera; no red clipping; 50 kB fits the Gen 1 link | Encoder too heavy for the MCUs; on the Pi Zero modular e7 doesn't fit and VarDCT e7 takes ~2 min/frame (on a crop it's cheaper: OQ-49 measured 1.6 s for 800×450) |
| **D-lin / D (grayscale JPEG per plane)** | Runs everywhere today (N6 hardware JPEG: 26 ms/frame) | Worse than today's JPEG on 8-bit OpenMV and at 50 kB on the IMX708 |
| **C (lossless packer) / N (near-lossless)** | MCU-proven (bit-exact on both boards), 2.6 KB working state | 1.9–3.4 bpp: only for "full RAW on command", not the routine link |
| **L (existing linear JPEG XL)** | Already in the repo; best "below noise" red at 0.8 bpp on IMX708 | Half resolution; same JPEG XL cost as D2 |

1. **IMX708 / Pi:** adopt **D2 on the field crop** (1600×900 → ~50 kB). Next measurement: D2 VarDCT and modular at effort 3–5 on the *crop* on the Zero (time, RSS), and on a 2×2-binned crop.
2. **N6 / AE3:** today they can only do **lossless (C)** or **D-lin** on-device. D2 needs a JPEG XL encoder on the MCU (libjxl-tiny or similar): a desk study first. D2 beats D by 26–87 %, so it is worth scoping. Until then, keep **C** for "RAW on command" (~2 bpp, 0.5–0.9 s).
3. Before any MCU decision: **get truly raw OpenMV data** (OQ-54: on-chip lens shading + denoise, 8-bit, black clipped). This needs your OK for sensor register writes.

## What I decided without you (please check)

- **OpenMV "raw" is processed 8-bit Bayer** (on-chip lens shading + denoise, black clipped). The spec says stop and ask; you'd asked me to continue, so OpenMV ran as its own class (OQ-54). Register reads only, no writes.
- **Underwater-sim** (thinning at capture) added as a second condition; the gate is reported for both.
- **M1-fix** added as the realistic camera baseline. Spec-M1 white-balances on the starved grey *before* 8-bit rounding, which flatters it.
- The card CCM is fitted on M0 to the V1 card's measured values. It is the same for every method, so absolute truth doesn't matter.
- GPL tools (x264, x265 via pillow-heif) ran only as internal Mac benchmarks, outside `src/` and outside `pyproject.toml` (study libs in the primary checkout's `.study-pylib/`). jpegli was built from libjxl v0.11.1 source.

## Not tested / limits

- In air under LEDs only; the "underwater" condition is simulated (no backscatter, no spectral change).
- 3 repeats per stop. Lamps were uneven (~25 % gradient) and clipped at stop 0, so stop −1 is the primary set; highlights are masked.
- OpenMV on-device sizes are from a dark scene (03:00), so only timings and bit-exactness carry over, not bytes.
- No INA3221 on this rig: energy comes from the UPS (whole rig, 10 mW–0.1 W resolution).
- x264 on 12 MP exceeds hardware H.264 levels (codec proxy only). Main profile has no 8×8 transform.
- The OpenMV USB console drops ~512-byte blocks under sustained output (OQ-55); the probe used CRC + 3 copies.
